traps: GAAP EPS of $2.46 is higher than non-GAAP EPS of $2.22 because GAAP includes $7,771 million of equity securities gains; swapping the labels or assuming adjusted is higher is the easiest error.
Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, non-GAAP measures no longer exclude stock-based compensation, and history was restated; comparing to older published non-GAAP figures is wrong.
Sequential vs year over year: revenue and Data Center are both up 18% from the previous quarter; 106% and 117% are the year-over-year rates. Edge Computing is 13% sequential, 27% year over year.
GAAP net income rose only 2% sequentially ($59,688 million vs $58,321 million) because the prior quarter carried $15,936 million of equity gains, while non-GAAP net income rose 18%.
Fiscal calendar: this is the second quarter of fiscal 2027 ended July 26, 2026, compared with the quarter ended July 27, 2025, not calendar Q2 2026 or fiscal 2026.
Quarter vs six months: statements carry six-month columns ($177,837 million revenue, $4.85 GAAP diluted EPS, $69,895 million free cash flow).
Units: tables are in millions; $96,221 million is $96.2 billion.

Cash flow: free cash flow of $21,341 million was up from $13,450 million a year ago but down from $48,554 million in the prior quarter, and GAAP net cash provided by operating activities of $24,077 million was far below net income of $59,688 million because accounts receivable rose by $22,346 million.

Balance sheet: the quarter included $24,896 million of debt issuance proceeds, and long-term debt was $32,366 million at July 26, 2026 vs $7,469 million at January 25, 2026, while the company returned approximately $26.0 billion to shareholders; the balance sheet compares with fiscal year end, not the prior quarter.

Gross margin was 75.0% on both GAAP and non-GAAP bases, but the year-over-year change is 2.6 pts GAAP and 2.5 pts non-GAAP; the third-quarter outlook of 74.0%, plus or minus 50 basis points, is a step down.

The outlook is for the third quarter only, excludes China Data Center compute revenue, and gives GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses of approximately $9.2 billion and $9.0 billion; there is no full-year revenue guidance.
The over $500 billion figure is third-party capital to be mobilized by financing partners over time, subject to definitive agreements; it is not NVIDIA revenue, backlog, or investment.
